key_insight: The paper introduces UniG2U-Bench, showing that unified generative multimodal models can help understanding in some-but-not-all scenarios by systematically categorizing generation-to-understanding (G2U) benefits across different task regimes.
problem_solved: Clarifies when and how generation improves multimodal understanding by providing a structured benchmark that fills gaps in existing evaluations, which lacked systematic exploration of tasks where generation aids understanding.
method: Construct UniG2U-Bench: a comprehensive benchmark that organizes G2U evaluation into 7 regimes and 30 subtasks.
Define tasks with varying degrees of implicit vs. explicit visual transformation to probe whether generation mechanisms help downstream understanding.
Provide standardized evaluation protocols to compare unified generative models on these diverse G2U subtasks.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to pinpoint which multimodal tasks benefit from generative capabilities, guiding model design, evaluation, and targeted improvements in unified models.
visual_elements: Overview diagram showing 7 G2U regimes arranged around a central unified model icon (radial layout).
Matrix or grid illustrating the 30 subtasks mapped by degree of visual transformation (implicit → explicit) and task type.
Example pipeline illustration: input image → generative transformation → understanding/answer, annotated with where generation helps or not.
Bar/heatmap comparing model performance across regimes to highlight strengths and gaps.
paper_title: UniG2U-Bench: Do Unified Models Advance Multimodal Understanding?
paper_authors: Zimo Wen, Boxiu Li, Wanbo Zhang, Junxiang Lei, Xiaoyu Chen
